title: Installer: generate .wxs into obj\ with deterministic component GUIDs (INST-4)

proposed_comments.title: Component identity and upgrade schedule
proposed_comments.body:
The generated WiX at lines 198–210 puts every file in `$fileList` into one component, with one registry value as the component key path. If one file is added or removed, this gives the entire component a new GUID, even though the remaining files, their destination paths, and the registry key path are unchanged. Windows Installer then sees the old and new GUIDs as different components that own overlapping resources.

This works with the current upgrade order: `Product.wxs:24` uses the default `MajorUpgrade` schedule, which removes the old product before installing the new one. It is not safe for the planned `afterInstallExecute` order. Under that order, the new component is installed first, and then uninstalling the old GUID can remove files or the registry value that the new component just installed.

I do not think there is a safe one-line code change here. Could we either generate stable components per installed file/path, or keep the current remove-first upgrade schedule and clarify that this PR does not yet enable `afterInstallExecute`? A two-version upgrade test where this file list changes would help validate whichever design we choose.

proposed_comments.title: Correct the module template directory
proposed_comments.body:
### Correct the module template directory

**Severity:** `low`

Step 2 points contributors to a directory that is absent from this installer tree, so following it puts `Module.wxs` outside the project. Please update it to the directory containing the existing WiX project and templates:

```suggestion
2. Inside `installer\PowerToysSetupVNext` add a new file for your module: `Module.wxs`
```

confidence.rationale: The pinned installer tree has the requested directory and project, but not the directory in this existing guide step; the exact replacement was applied and checked. The PR updates this same onboarding procedure immediately around the stale step.
